html:
Taiwan's first farmers were Austronesian speaking peoples who crossed from the coast of mainland China more than 5,000 years ago. Their descendants are Taiwan's indigenous peoples.

Taiwan holds nine of the ten main branches of the Austronesian language family, more than all the rest of the world together. That is why most scholars see it as the family's homeland. From about 3000 BCE groups sailed south to the Philippines and on through Indonesia, out into the Pacific and as far as Madagascar, a spread told in the settlement of the Philippines and of Polynesia.

On Taiwan itself the tribes lived alone for thousands of years, until Chinese and Dutch settlers came in the 17th century and pushed them into the mountains. Today they are a little over 2 per cent of the people, with 16 recognised peoples, and since the 1990s Taiwan has stressed this heritage as part of what makes it distinct from China.
sum: Taiwan's first farmers were Austronesian speaking peoples who crossed from the coast of mainland China more than 5,000 years ago. Their descendants are Taiwan's indigenous peoples.
